96: // Function maps OTel severity on the LogRecord to DataSet severity level (number)
97: func otelSeverityToDataSetSeverity(log plog.LogRecord) int {
98: 	// If log record doesn't contain severity or we can't map it to a valid DataSet severity,
99: 	// we use this value (INFO) instead
100: 	defaultSeverityLevel := 3
101: 
102: 	// This function maps OTel severity level to DataSet severity levels
103: 	//
104: 	// Valid OTel levels - https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/logs/data-model/#field-severitynumber
105: 	// and valid DataSet ones - https://github.com/scalyr/logstash-output-scalyr/blob/master/lib/logstash/outputs/scalyr.rb#L70
106: 	sevNum := log.SeverityNumber()
107: 	sevText := log.SeverityText()
108: 
109: 	dataSetSeverity := defaultSeverityLevel
110: 
111: 	if sevNum > 0 {
112: 		dataSetSeverity = otelSeverityNumberToDataSetSeverity(sevNum, defaultSeverityLevel)
113: 	} else if sevText != "" {
114: 		// Per docs, SeverityNumber is optional so if it's not present we fall back to SeverityText
115: 		// https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/logs/data-model/#field-severitytext
116: 		switch strings.ToLower(sevText) {
117: 		case "fine", "finest":
118: 			dataSetSeverity = 0
119: 		case "trace":
120: 			dataSetSeverity = 1
121: 		case "debug":
122: 			dataSetSeverity = 2
123: 		case "info", "information":
124: 			dataSetSeverity = 3
125: 		case "warn", "warning":
126: 			dataSetSeverity = 4
127: 		case "error":
128: 			dataSetSeverity = 5
129: 		case "fatal", "critical", "emergency":
130: 			dataSetSeverity = 6
131: 		}
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	// TODO: We should log in case we see invalid severity, but right now, afaik, we / OTEL
135: 	// don't have a concept of "rate limited" logging. We don't want to log every single
136: 	// occurrence in case there are many log records like that since this could cause a lot of
137: 	// noise and performance overhead
138: 
139: 	return dataSetSeverity
140: }
